questions.q: Does Section 40 sickness compensation reach informal workers diagnosed with heat illness?
questions.have: Current benefit changes are published; heat-specific applications and payments were not verified. [T3]
questions.could: Prospective claims-pathway study tracking aggregate awareness, documentation, accepted claims, value and delay.
questions.scale: Illustrative: several provinces over two hot seasons; final size based on case flow.

questions.q: Does heat-triggered insurance preserve earnings and reduce debt without changing essential work hours?
questions.have: A worker-network pilot and partner reports exist without an independent impact estimate. [T15, T16]
questions.could: Pre-registered phased rollout with agreed comparison clusters, measuring income, care costs, rest and coping in aggregate.
questions.scale: Illustrative: 40-60 clusters across two hot seasons.

questions.q: How different are social-insurance coverage maps based on residence and employer registration?
questions.have: SSO metadata describes different location concepts by section. [T11]
questions.could: Secure institutional aggregation of both location definitions; publish only province-level differences and uncertainty.
questions.scale: Illustrative: one year of all available provincial aggregate records.

questions.q: How much heat-related crop loss is met by declared-disaster relief, and how quickly?
questions.have: Crop-relief rates, documents and procedure are published. [T5]
questions.could: Crop-season household panel and administrative aggregate audit of declarations, assessed losses, payment dates and recovery.
questions.scale: Illustrative: 1,000-1,500 households across several agroclimatic areas.

evidence.title: HomeNet Thailand Runs a Pilot Extreme Heat Insurance Project for Informal Economy Workers
evidence.scale: Self-reported pilot for 1,000 informal workers, May-July 2026
evidence.finding: UNCERTAIN self-report: a heat-triggered insurance pilot offered THB300 daily assistance against a THB100 contribution. Payout triggers were reportedly reached in some provinces; no independently measured household effect was read.
evidence.limit: The policy contract and final evaluation were not opened; inconsistent payout-cap wording prevents a reliable total payout-day claim.

evidence.finding: UNCERTAIN self-reported experiences: women described heat-related earnings and health pressures. The summary identifies a shock pathway, without estimating an insurance or public-transfer effect.
evidence.limit: Own partner summary only; full report methods and its own stated limits were not verified because the attachment was too large for the reader.

indicators.indicator: Days with daily maximum air temperature above 35 degrees C
indicators.definition: Proposed annual count from ERA5 hourly 2 m air temperature, using local calendar days. Threshold is an analytical choice, not a national warning or safe-work limit.
indicators.limit: INFERRED; native 0.25 degree grid. No country values calculated. Use correct local time zones. [Te]

indicators.indicator: Days with daily minimum air temperature above 28 degrees C
indicators.definition: Proposed annual count from the same temperature series. A whole-day minimum is a reproducible hot-night proxy, not a measured sleeping condition.
indicators.place_code: Same grid and selected boundary as hotdays
indicators.limit: INFERRED; indoor heat, wind, work intensity and radiant heat are not measured. [Te]

indicators.definition: Proposed annual mean of hourly 2 m dew-point temperature, aggregated by area. It gives moisture context rather than a validated humid-heat health index.
indicators.place_code: Same grid and boundary as hotdays
indicators.limit: INFERRED; dew point is not wet-bulb temperature, heat index or WBGT. [Te]

indicators.definition: Proposed sum of the published age-sex raster bands aged 65+ divided by the total for the same release.
indicators.licence: CC BY 4.0 stated; check file provenance for ODbL exception
indicators.limit: INFERRED, not census counts; about 100 m native grid. Administrative aggregates not downloaded or calculated. [Tw]

indicators.limit: INFERRED; age-group labels and totals receive a check before calculation. This is not eligibility for a child benefit. [Tw]
